Academic Subjects Drama and Theatre Studies
Drama and Theatre Studies
The study of Drama at St Edward’s is greatly enhanced by the presence on school grounds of The North Wall, a highly-regarded arts centre with its own theatre which is also home to the School’s Drama and Dance Departments.
Owned and managed by the School, The North Wall runs a public programme which brings professional performers, writers, directors and technicians into pupils’ day-to-day lives, giving them an unparalleled opportunity to experience and learn.
Pupils in the Shell can choose Drama as one of their optional subjects and are introduced to a wide range of theatre. Drama helps pupils develop confidence through teamwork, collaboration and performance.
In the Fourth and Fifth Form the Drama Pathway features practical workshops and creative projects which allow pupils to experience drama and theatre as performers, designers and directors. We help them expand their ability to respond critically and sensitively to a range of drama texts and to live theatre.
An A Level course sees pupils take on roles within two examined performance pieces. One is a devised piece and the other is an extract from a published play. The written exam is comprised of one section on productions the pupils have seen and two sections on plays they have studied.
The IB Theatre Arts course is an exciting and organic course that allows pupils the chance to explore a wide range of theatre practice from around the world. The IB is a very practical course underpinned by academic research.
Pupils from all year groups can audition for and take part in the School’s productions – from Shakespeare plays to musicals. There are many opportunities for taking on technical roles in these productions and pupils develop expertise in lighting, sound and costume design. Each year Sixth Formers take a production to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival.
Director of Drama: Katrina Eden
Head of Academic Drama: Alice Kenny

pageCache.text:
Academic Subjects Computer Science
Computer Science
Computer Science allows pupils to explore how computers define the world we live in. Through studying computers and computational systems, their theory, design and application, pupils will develop the skills they will need to solve problems using technology.
Pupils can choose Computer Science as an option in the Shell when the focus of the course is on coding and programming to solve real world problems in the School and the community. Pupils tackle practical tasks individually and in small groups. Building adaptive greenhouses that can detect temperature and climactic conditions is just one example of the sort of project they engage with.
The GCSE course covers computational thinking, code training, problem-solving, programming concepts and coding. Pupils learn about the theoretical side of computer science and learn about computing concepts which underpin how modern systems work.
At A Level the syllabus has a focus on programming as well as theoretical knowledge. Pupils learn how to code and program in a variety of languages and how computers work and communicate with each other. They learn about the process of writing software and developing an idea into a working application.
Head of Department: Jonathan Hooper

Academic Subjects Art, Ceramics and Photography
Art, Ceramics and Photography
Art is a way of developing a visual language and fostering the creative process through discussion, understanding, communication, and realisation of ideas.
In the Fourth and Fifth Form we offer our own St Edward’s Pathways and Perspectives course in Art as well as GCSE Ceramics.
In the Sixth Form pupils can study A Level in Fine Art, Textiles, or Photography or choose Visual Arts as one of their IB subjects.
Our teachers are highly-skilled, practising artists in a wide range of disciplines. Learning and teaching takes place in a variety of ways, including one-to-one tutorials, group discussions and skills workshops. We encourage our pupils to identify and exploit their own expressive potential, creating opportunities for experimental work across multiple disciplines including drawing and painting, photography, textiles, silk screen printing, etching, ceramics, laser cutting, and digital media.
Pupils are encouraged to find their individual language and make connections between visual, written and contextual sources.
We believe that drawing in the broadest sense is fundamental and it is encouraged across all year groups. This is the core of all artistic practice and is nurtured and developed through experience, learning and a variety of techniques. The department’s weekly life drawing classes are an excellent platform for all pupils to develop their observational drawing skills.
We have excellent facilities with a photography lighting studio, a digital editing suite, a dedicated ceramics studio with three large kilns and potter’s wheels, allowing pupils to create a wide range of two-dimensional and three-dimensional work. The etching press, laser cutter and the photo-sensitive silkscreen facilities are popular with pupils.
Our pupils’ work is regularly exhibited for public viewing in The North Wall Gallery.
Head of Department: Adam Hahn

Academic Subjects Biology
Biology
Biology is a rapidly expanding and fascinating subject. Recent advances in molecular biology, biochemistry and the new science of epigenetics have brought with them an ever-increasing range of career opportunities with exciting possibilities in many fields including medicine, forensic science, developmental biology and agriculture.
At St Edward’s we consider a practical approach to biology to be the best foundation for further study, as well as being the best way to stimulate interest in, and enjoyment of, the subject.
Our choice of courses reflects this philosophy. At GCSE pupils study Biology as part of their Double or Triple Science Award. In the Sixth Form pupils can study Biology at A Level or as an IB (Standard or Higher Level).
Sixth Form pupils frequently opt to write IB Extended Essays on subjects related to Biology and are well supported by our experienced team of teachers and technicians. All our IB pupils take part in a five-day ecology field course, gaining hands-on experience of data collection.
The Biology Department runs a Biology Society which publishes a twice-yearly magazine ‘Teddies Talks’ and Goodall Society, an academically challenging discussion group. Local scientists frequently come to School to give lectures and we host an annual Biology Symposium focusing on cutting-edge science, in collaboration with the Oxford International Biomedical Centre.
Head of Department: Dr Karla Perera

Academic Subjects Chemistry
Chemistry
The study and practice of Chemistry have played, and continue to play, a major role in shaping our civilisation. It is the central science.
At the physical end of the spectrum Chemistry ties in with a great deal of research in Physics and Engineering, and at the Biochemical end there is vital overlap in areas such as medicine design and synthesis.
At St Edward’s we try to make pupils aware of the effects Chemistry has in the world around us. In the Shell it is a core subject and pupils are taught about the particle model of matter, the formation of compounds and chemical reactions. Pupils learn accurate scientific vocabulary and chemical symbolism, allowing them to represent and explain chemical behaviour. This feeds into the GCSE course, with pupils studying Chemistry as part of their Double or Triple Science Award.
In the Sixth Form pupils can choose to take Chemistry as an A Level or IB course. The A Level course covers all the major aspects of Chemistry, including its uses within medicine and industry. The IB syllabus focuses on the investigative nature of Chemistry and in the Upper Sixth pupils devise and carry out their own scientific investigation.
Learning in the classroom is complemented by trips to see the many and varied applications of chemistry, such as visiting Syngenta to find out about their work on pesticides and plant breeding and the National Gallery to find out about art restoration methods. We also enter a countywide Chemist of the Year award, the Chemistry Olympiad, as well as various national Chemistry competitions. For the Lower Sixth, there is the Priestley Society and for the Upper Sixth the Cavendish Society, and we have a very active Medicine Society with many speakers from Oxford University and its hospitals.
Head of Department: Dr Matthew Fletcher

Academic Subjects Design Technology and Jewellery
Design Technology and Jewellery
Design & Technology at St. Edward’s is ambitious and future facing. The department teaches pupils to think independently, solve complex problems and turn ideas into high-quality, tangible outcomes.
Through a combination of traditional craftsmanship, cutting-edge technology and entrepreneurial thinking, pupils learn to design with purpose and intent and to develop their creativity.
The Design & Technology Department is housed in purpose-built studios and workshops with industry-standard facilities. Pupils have access to advanced CAD/CAM provision, CNC machinery, laser and plasma cutting, 3D scanning, vacuum casting and additive manufacture.
Design is available from the Shell, where pupils build a strong foundation in traditional craftsmanship alongside the intelligent application of emerging technologies. Pupils develop ideas through iterative modelling, CAD software and rapid prototyping, learning to think like designers from the outset.
In the Fourth and Fifth Form pupils can choose a Design and Entrepreneurship Pathway or Jewellery and Entrepreneurship Pathway, both combining hands-on making with developing business acumen, branding and marketing skills. The Design and Entrepreneurship Pathway explores at architecture, product design and engineering, and concludes in the development of a viable design or business concept. The Jewellery and Entrepreneurship Pathway allows pupils to learn traditional silversmithing techniques such as stone-setting, soldering, casting, riveting and enamelling. Pupils combine these practical skills with business knowledge to consider how they would build a jewellery collection and brand.
In the Sixth Form, pupils may study IB Design Technology, A Level Product Design, or A Level Jewellery.
A Level Jewellery offers pupils the opportunity to specialise in designing and making high quality pieces. Pupils develop an understanding of materials, processes and craftsmanship and are encouraged to think about their work within wider design, cultural and commercial contexts.
A Level Product Design focuses on technical depth, creativity and problem-solving through iterative design and manufacture. Pupils develop advanced skills in modelling, prototyping and making, learning about materials, processes and industrial manufacture.
IB Design Technology develops reflective, globally-minded designers who place the user at the centre of the design process. Pupils explore human-centred design and sustainability and ethical practice.
Pupils with a particular passion for design are encouraged to extend their learning beyond the curriculum. The School’s Design Society offers opportunities to work on real briefs for external clients, while the Architecture Society explores architectural history and contemporary practice in greater depth.
Head of Department: Andrew Halliwell

Academic Subjects English
English
The English Department aims to encourage a love of literature and an appreciation of imaginative, original and expressive writing.
English plays a key role in promoting intellectual curiosity and academic attainment across the curriculum.
Considerable emphasis is placed on accuracy and discernment in the use of the English language and pupils leave St Edward’s equipped to express their ideas with passion, articulacy and confidence. Pupils are encouraged to read widely, with intelligence, enthusiasm and discrimination, and to be lucid and articulate in class discussions and on paper.
In the Shell pupils the curriculum embraces contemporary authors and the study of the classics, including Dickens and a Shakespeare play. All pupils then take English Language and World Literature at GCSE.
At Sixth Form pupils can choose to study English Literature as an IB (Higher or Standard Level) or A Level course. Both courses develop skills of critical analysis and look at drama, poetry and prose, investigating the ideas and society of their authors.
The School’s literary society, the Phoenix Society, regularly invites authors, directors, performers and distinguished academics to talk to pupils. We also arrange cultural trips to Stratford-upon-Avon, the Ashmolean, the Globe, Covent Garden and the theatres of the West End.
Head of Department: Jason Edward Clapham

Academic Subjects Geography
Geography
With growing interest in issues such as climate change, migration, environmental degradation and social cohesion, Geography is one of the most relevant subjects a young person can choose to study.
The Geography Department aims to prepare pupils to engage with the world equipped with the knowledge and skills to better understand their surroundings.
All pupils take Geography in the Shell year, where we study a number of contemporary topics. During this year pupils should expect to explore the ways societies, economies and cultures are linked across the world, investigate issues of food production and supply, consider how places can evoke contrasting feelings for different people, and analyse how Geography can affect conflicts.
In the Fourth and Fifth pupils can choose to take Geography as a GCSE or the Sustainability Pathway. The GCSE course studies the characteristics and processes taking place within physical and human environments, encouraging pupils to analyse important issues and viewpoints. The Sustainability Pathway explores the natural environment and the challenge posed by factors such as climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution. Pupils consider possible solutions to address and mitigate these global issues.
At Sixth Form pupils select either the A Level or IB programme. Both courses develop a broad spectrum of knowledge and understanding. They discover, for example, the features of our human and physical landscapes and the differences and inequality within the human world. They learn how to observe, describe, analyse, represent, interpret and report information about the world and how it operates as an integrated system.
Fieldwork is an essential part of the study of Geography and recent trips in the UK have included visits to Dorset the London Olympic Park. In the Sixth Form, A Level and IB pupils take part in a residential field trip to South Wales.
The department boasts a thriving Geography Society which helps to enhance pupils’ knowledge and understanding of the geographical world. The department is able to make use of the school’s location within Oxford to invite academics from the local universities to speak.
Head of Department: Dr Emily Bernstein

Academic Subjects History
History
History illuminates the past and gives meaning to the present. An education in history is fundamental to understanding the world in which we live and helps to meet the demand for greater social awareness in society. In an age saturated with information, History provides the knowledge and tools to navigate the 21st century, not just the past.
In the Shell year pupils start with a History of St Edward’s before studying topics including WWI, the Russian Revolution, and the Slave Trade.
In the Fourth and Fifth Form History is offered as an option at GCSE. The course looks at Germany 1918-45, the USA 1918-41, the USSR 1924-53, and China 1900-89.
In the Sixth Form, pupils can choose either the IB or A Level course. At IB pupils study topics including the French Revolution, Napoleon, and Authoritarian States. The source paper examines post-war Europe 1945-60 and the Indochina Refugee Crisis 1975-1990. At A Level pupils study three topics: British History in the 19th or 20th century, the American or French Revolution, and a breadth study of either Medieval Heresy or Tudor Rebellions. Pupils also submit a coursework essay on Alfred the Great. Many A Level and IB pupils complete an Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) or IB Extended Essay in a history-related topic.
History at St Edward’s goes far beyond the classroom and there are two flourishing History societies. The first is the Blenheim Society which is open to all Sixth Form historians and encourages pupil participation.
The History society hosts prestigious speakers and also includes forums, discussions, and talks. Recent subjects have included the nature of medieval heresy, sixteenth-century witchcraft, nationalism and the Rwandan genocide. The Gibson Society is an exciting way for Lower School pupils to develop their interest in the past. Activities include assessing the historical accuracy of Hollywood movies, researching family history, and delving into historical fiction.
Head of Department: Henry Moore

pageCache.pageTitle: Space, Time and Shakespeare | St Edwards School Oxford
pageCache.text:
Space, Time and Shakespeare
On Wednesday, the Lower Sixth A Level mathematicians attended a lecture from Dr Paul Glendinning at the University of Oxford. The lecture discussed the technological advancements and mathematical processes of the late Tudor and early Jacobean period and how these were utilised in Shakespeare’s literary works.
Similarly to a Shakespearean play, the lecture was divided into five acts examining, military application of Jacob’s Technique in Henry IV, the mechanical use of an almanac to read the phases of the moon in A Midsummer Night’s Dream, the increase in the use of mirrors and the influence this had on the writing of Macbeth, the measuring of solar and lunar calendars in Julius Caesar and finally the Bard’s admiration for the increase in technology in ‘Sonnet 77’. It was a very enjoyable lecture, creating synoptic links between maths, english and history.
Thy glass will show thee how thy beauties wear, Thy dial how thy precious minutes waste; The vacant leaves thy mind’s imprint will bear, And of this book, this learning mayst thou taste. The wrinkles which thy glass will truly show Of mouthed graves will give thee memory; Thou by thy dial’s shady stealth mayst know Time’s thievish progress to eternity. Look what thy memory cannot contain, Commit to these waste blanks, and thou shalt find Those children nursed, deliver’d from thy brain, To take a new acquaintance of thy mind. These offices, so oft as thou wilt look, Shall profit thee and much enrich thy book.
Report written by Lower Sixth pupil, Blake Maddox

About Us International Partnerships
International Partnerships
St Edward’s Oxford, has a long tradition of looking outwards, welcoming diverse perspectives, forging global relationships, and preparing young people to thrive in an interconnected world. Building on this heritage, we are actively developing opportunities to extend the Teddies ethos and educational model internationally.
Expanding the Teddies Vision Worldwide
Today, our global footprint includes established exchange programmes and collaborative relationships in India, South Africa, the USA, Germany and New Zealand, with additional partnerships in advanced stages of development.
We are also proud that 25% of our pupils join us from over 44 different countries, enriching our community with a vast range of cultures, interests and viewpoints. These connections deepen our pupils’ experiences and reflect our commitment to broad, globally minded education.

Academic Subjects Classics
Classics
The study of Classics encompasses literature, history, art, archaeology, philosophy, and linguistics. Pupils learn how ancient civilisations have shaped the modern world through their languages, myths, aesthetics, writers and philosophers.
All Shell pupils study Classics as one of their core subjects and learn to engage critically with literary, epigraphic and archaeological evidence as well as learning Latin.
Those who select the School’s Ancient World Perspective in the Fourth and Fifth Form address questions such as, ‘What makes a hero?’, ‘Why do empires fall?’ and ‘Why do those in power seek to conquer others?’. They also consider our enduring fascination with myths, studying both Greek and Roman epics and the modern iconography of superheroes and the Marvel Universe. Pupils can also choose to study Ancient Greek and Latin at GCSE, focusing on their language and profound literature.
In the Sixth Form, pupils can choose to study Classical Civilisation, Latin and/or Greek at A Level or as Classical Languages in the IB Diploma. Classical Civilisation A Level focuses on the literature and material culture of Greece, including topics on Greek Religion and The Invention of the Barbaria. All these courses aim to develop a level of competence in Latin or Classical Greek to allow pupils to read and understand ancient texts with immediacy and understanding.
Pupils make trips to Romano-British settlements, enter essay and reading competitions, attend course-related conferences and exhibitions and live performances of Greek drama. We also run a biennial trip to ancient sites in Europe, recently to Sicily and Rome itself. We greatly benefit from our location in Oxford: there are visits to the Ashmolean, and our active Lyne Society hosts university dons and other eminent classicists. The junior branch of this society (Lower Lyne) is run by Sixth Formers who organise monthly quizzes, debates, sculpture workshops and films.
Head of Department: Mark Taylor

Academic Subjects Dance
Dance
In the Sixth Form pupils can take Dance as an IB course at either Standard or Higher Level.
Our co-curricular Dance offering has always been superb, with around a quarter of pupils in the school taking dance and performing at an incredibly high level.
Studying Dance as part of their IB Diploma allows pupils to learn more about choreography and the history of dance.
Pupils analyse and reflect on dance practices, for example comparing dances with folkloric traditions such as flamenco with classical ballet. They learn leadership skills in choreographing and leading their peers and collaboration as they work together to refine a performance in rehearsals. They can also use the extra lesson time in the Dance Studios to hone their own technique, with 40% of the grade awarded for performance.
Head of Department: Lisa Elkins

Academic Subjects Economics and Business Studies
Economics and Business Studies
Economics is a social science that studies almost every aspect of human life: economists are interested in the systems that shape our decisions, and the results of these decisions.
In microeconomics, we study how households and firms interact to produce and consume goods and services, as well as how and why the government may choose to get involved. Macroeconomics looks at the big picture, addressing some of the most significant issues facing countries today: how do we increase growth rates? How should we tackle income inequality? How important is international trade?
We offer Economics as an A Level and IB option in the Sixth Form. In both courses, pupils develop an understanding of technical economic models, and then apply them to a range of real-world situations, with a focus on evaluating economic theories and policies.
We also offer an A Level in Business, which looks at how modern organisations operate. Pupils study business decisions, resource management, marketing strategies and the globalised business environment. The course is very applied, leaning heavily on case studies, and helps pupils develop their own entrepreneurial skills. There are plenty of opportunities within the department to learn about Economics and Business beyond the courses.
An Economics Society meets fortnightly to explore big questions in economics and discuss recent research. The pupil-led Business Society gives pupils an opportunity to develop more real-world business experience. The School’s Financial Markets Society allows pupils to work towards a qualification with the Chartered Institute of Securities and Investments.
Head of Department: Mark Austen

pageCache.pageTitle: A Level Results 2026 | St Edwards School Oxford
pageCache.text:
A Level Results 2026
Congratulations to Teddies’ A Level pupils, who received a hugely impressive set of results, matching the success of IB pupils earlier in the summer.
82% of all grades are at A*-B, six percentage points up on the same time last year. The combined figure, including the Higher Level IB grades achieved in July at 7-5, is 84% – which makes 2026 one of the most successful summers on record and a great testament to the hard work of this cohort of pupils and their teachers. Equally impressive is that nearly half of all grades (48%) across Higher Level IB and A Level are at the very top end, at A*/A or 7/6. The A* rate in the A Level results stands at 15.4%, which is four percentage points higher than last year and, excepting the years in which grading was affected by the pandemic, the highest level achieved in the last ten years.
Alastair Chirnside, the Warden, said, ‘This is a remarkable set of results, and I could not be more proud of our pupils. It must be remembered that alongside all the hard work required to achieve these results, last year’s leavers made a wonderful and inspiring contribution to the rich life of the School across the board – in concerts, plays and dance shows, through their involvement in sport – often at elite level – and by taking on demanding leadership and community volunteering roles. The dedication, energy and enthusiasm required to succeed and to be fulfilled in all areas of school life are the hallmarks of a Teddies education. I am delighted to see it so brilliantly demonstrated by our 2026 leavers.’
Since IB results were announced in July, reviews of the marking have increased the proportion of Higher Level grades at Levels 7-5 to 92%, which sets a new record for the School. More than 40% of the cohort achieved 38 points or more, broadly equivalent to A*AA. One pupil has secured the maximum of 45 points, an extremely rare feat achieved by less than 1% of the 200,000 pupils who study the IB internationally.
These outstanding results will take Teddies pupils to the world’s best universities, including Oxford, Cambridge, Durham, Imperial College London, King’s College London, Edinburgh, Manchester and Warwick in the UK, and Harvard, Columbia, Cornell, New York University, Georgetown and UCAL San Diego in the US. Pupils will also take up places at McGill in Canada and at the University of Sydney in Australia, with places at Trinity College Dublin set to be confirmed by the end of this month. As ever, Teddies pupils go on to study an extraordinary range of subjects including Medicine, Veterinary Science, Architecture, Engineering, Music, Chemistry, Fine Art, Filmmaking, Maritime Engineering, Agricultural Business Management and Fashion Marketing – among many others.
We wish our 2026 leavers every success as they prepare for university, for gap years, and for the wide variety of their future endeavours – and we look forward to welcoming them back to Teddies as OSE soon and often.

Academic Careers & Futures
Careers & Futures
The Careers Programme at St Edward’s is designed to support pupils throughout their academic journey, from the Shell to Upper Sixth. It provides a structured framework that equips pupils with the necessary skills and knowledge to make informed decisions about their future careers.
Pupils in all years are entitled to access to the careers provisions and impartial careers advice to support them in their decision making.
Our Careers Department offers:
Impartial Guidance
The programme is delivered in an impartial, unbiased and information-led manner, with each year group building upon the knowledge and skills acquired in the previous years.
Individualised Support
The Careers Centre offers personalised guidance through one-on-one consultations and drop-in clinics. All pupils can arrange to see the Level 6 qualified Careers Advisor or Head of Careers as and when needed.
Exploration and Discovery
Pupils are encouraged to explore their interests, strengths, and values to identify suitable career paths.
Actionable Skills Development
The programme equips pupils with practical skills such as CV writing, interview techniques, and networking.
Planning for the Future
The Careers Department work with pupils throughout their time at St Edward’s, ensuring that the decisions they make about their future are carefully considered and planned. This guidance is structured as follows:
Shell
Individual consultations to discuss GCSE course selection
Fourth Form
Fifth Form
Lower Sixth
One-to-one conversation with the Careers Advisor
Upper Sixth
Additional Resources
The Careers Department organises regular talks and workshops. These Inspiring Futures talks feature professionals from a range of backgrounds, from design and marketing to engineering and tech. These talks complement the super-curricular lectures organised by academic subject departments.
A dedicated careers library is available within the Careers Centre.
The Careers Centre is conveniently located in the heart of the school and is easily accessible by pupils.
We encourage our pupils to actively engage with the Careers Programme and take advantage of the various resources available. If you have any questions or suggestions, please do not hesitate to contact the Careers Department at careerseducation@stedwardsoxford.org.
